thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: pd_incident #12345 - service=inference-prod - symptom=high tail latency (>10s) - region=us-east-prod. Automated page to on-call. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/inference-latency

pagerduty: Details: service=inference-prod, severity=high, 95th latency=12.4s, 5xx rate=0.2%, triggered 5m ago. Affected cluster: us-east-a. Link to traces: https://traces/redwood/12345

jordan_oncall: ack — I'm on it. :wave: starting quick triage, will post updates.

alice: thanks — I'm available to help with routing if needed. Any customer hits so far?

jordan_oncall: initial signal: latency spike concentrated in us-east-a nodes. Dashboard shows GPU util ~98% on a subset of nodes, queue depth high. Checking pods now.

ben: querying logs: `kubectl -n inference logs deploy/serve-v2 -c runtime --since=10m | grep "connection reset"` shows repeated connection resets from model runtime on node-gpu-14.

omar_eng: Envoy metrics show long request queue_time, KV-cache evictions spiking at same time -> possible cache thrash under high concurrency.

jordan_oncall: health endpoints respond OK but warm-up latency is high. Running quick `top` on node-gpu-14 — GPU mem fully occupied.

kate_cs: FYI I've got a ticket from Acme Mobile reporting elevated latency to their end-users around the time of the page.

alice: can we quantify customer impact? traces?

jordan_oncall: traces show ~5 timed-out requests from Acme in last 10m. Severity small but visible.

jordan_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) scale up replicas in affected pool, 2) reroute high-latency customer traffic to us-west while new capacity warms, 3) avoid scheduling on suspected bad node(s). Executing scale now.

ben: `kubectl scale deployment/serve-v2 --replicas=12 -n inference` — scaled, pods creating. I'll monitor readiness.

omar_eng: autoscaler config note: min=4 max=20 target_cpu=70 — looks like burst didn't trigger because the metric smoothing window is 3m. We'll investigate after.

incident-bot: Action: started warm replicas in us-east (4) and queued routing change to shift traffic to us-west for critical customers.

ben: New pods ready ~38s ago. Early signs: queue depth dropped on new pods.

jordan_oncall: after scale+reroute: 95th latency down to ~2.1s, 5xx back to baseline. Continuing to monitor.

kate_cs: pinged Acme: "We see improvement on our side; please let us know if you still see issues." They replied acknowledging improvement.

alice: notes for postmortem: suspected contributors = GPU saturation, KV-cache eviction thrash, autoscaler smoothing window too long for this workload.

omar_eng: capturing heap/profile snapshots from affected pods; scheduling `gcore` and saving logs to ENG-4521.

jordan_oncall: I'll post status pings every 10m. Next check in ~10m.

incident-bot: pd_incident #12345 status=ack by jordan_oncall. Timeline recorded.

jordan_oncall: (10m update) system stable; latency within SLO across regions. Keeping the page open for 30m to ensure stability.

ben: observed some earlier OOM kills on node-gpu-14; I've temporarily tainted node-gpu-14 to avoid new scheduling: `kubectl taint nodes node-gpu-14 avoid-scheduling=true:NoSchedule`.

kate_cs: Acme confirms improved performance; will reopen if they see regressions.

alice: assigning eng-runtime for follow-up tuning (autoscaler and kv-cache). @omar_eng please own RCA.

omar_eng: taking it — creating ENG-4521 with traces, heap dumps, and timeline.

jordan_oncall: handoff: oncall releasing incident to Omar for RCA/work items. I'll keep monitoring until automated resolve.

incident-bot: pd_incident #12345 -> escalated to ENG owner=omar_eng for RCA. Page will auto-resolve if no further alerts in 30m."
